items.actClause: AN ACT to authorize the town of Southeast, in the county of Putnam, to issue bonds for certain extraordinary expenses incurred by the Springhouse water district
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5429

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to authorize the town of Southeast, in the
county of Putnam, to issue bonds for certain extraordinary expenses
incurred by the Springhouse water district

PURPOSE: To authorize the issuance of serial bonds for the town of
Southeast, in the county of Putnam, to repay its general fund for
extraordinary expenses on behalf of the Springhouse water district.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:  The town of Southeast, in the county of
Putnam, is authorized to issue serial bonds on or before December 31,
2015 in an aggregate principal amount not to exceed $380,000 for
extraordinary expenses incurred by the town on behalf of the
Springhouse water district after the district's then-existing water
supply source was declared unsafe by the department of health and
before a new permanent water supply system could be designed and
constructed. "Extraordinary expenses" as used in this section mean
those operating and capital costs related to the operation of the
district's water supply system with water supplied by tank truck and
with the use of a temporary water purification system, including water
delivery charges and waste water pumping charges, as well as other
related town costs incurred to acquire and construct a new water
supply system that were not reimbursed to the town through its
financings with the New York state environmental facilities
corporation on May 9 2013 and July 2, 2014.  The period of probable
usefulness of such objects or purposes shall be thirty years.

JUSTIFICATION:  Following the Department of Health's determination
that the Springhouse water district's supply was unsafe, it took the
town of Southeast approximately five years to develop plans, receive
regulatory approval, obtain low cost financing and construct a new
permanent water supply system. During this lengthy period, the Town
incurred approximately $380,000 of extraordinary expenses for
operating and capital costs relating to water acquisition,
purification and disposal of water purification waste water, as well
as other related costs incurred to acquire and construct a new water
supply system. This bill would authorize the town to issue bonds to
repay its general fund for the extraordinary expenses incurred on
behalf of the water district for a term of up to thirty years in order
to minimize the fiscal impact on the water district's residents.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY: New bill

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS: None to the state

EFFECTIVE DATE: Immediately.

B.actClause: AN ACT to authorize the town of Southeast, in the county of Putnam, to issue bonds for certain extraordinary expenses incurred by the Springhouse water district
B.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S5429B

TITLE OF BILL:  An act to authorize the town of Southeast, in the
county of Putnam, to issue bonds for certain extraordinary expenses
incurred by the Springhouse water district

PURPOSE:

To authorize the issuance of serial bonds for the town of Southeast,
in the county of Putnam, to repay its general fund for extraordinary
expenses on behalf of the Springhouse water district.

SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS:

Section 1. The Town of Southeast, in the county of Putnam, is hereby
authorized to issue serial bonds, subject to the provisions of this
act, on or before December 31, 2015, for the specific object or
purpose of reimbursing the town for payments made by the town from the
town general fund on behalf of the Springhouse Water District for the
extraordinary expenses incurred by the town on behalf of the district
after the district's then existing water supply source was declared
unsafe by the department of health and before a new, permanent water
supply system could be designed and constructed.  "Extraordinary
expenses" as used in this section shall mean those operating and
capital costs related to the operation of the district's water supply
system with water supplied by tank truck and with water supplied using
a temporary water purification system, including water delivery
charges and water pumping charges, as well as other related town costs
incurred to acquire and construct a new water supply system that were
not reimbursed to the town through its financings with the New York
State Environmental Facilities Corporation on May 9, 2013 and July 2,
2014.

§ 2. Notwithstanding the provisions of section 11.00 of the local
finance law, the specific object or purpose referred to in section one
of this act is hereby declared to be a public purpose which the Town
of Southeast is hereby authorized to accomplish with the issuance of
serial bonds in an aggregate principal amount not to exceed three
hundred and eighty thousand dollars ($380,000); provided, that no such
bonds to reimburse the town for the extraordinary expenses incurred
shall be issued until the state comptroller shall first review and
confirm the actual amount of the extraordinary expenses, and that the
amount of such bonds issued to reimburse the town for the
extraordinary expenses incurred shall not exceed the amount certified
by the state comptroller. There period of probable usefulness of the
serial bonds issued pursuant to this act is hereby authorized to be
twenty-five years.

§ 3. The Town of Southeast is hereby authorized to levy an annual tax
on the properties of the district in an amount sufficient to pay the
annual debt service on such serial bonds. Such tax shall be levied
against each individual property in the district using the same
formula by which other district assessments are levied.

§ 4. In anticipation of the issuance and sale of such serial bonds,
the Town of Southeast is hereby authorized to issue bond anticipation
notes in accordance with the provisions of the Local Finance Law.


JUSTIFICATION:

Following the Department of Health's determination that the
Springhouse water district's supply was unsafe, it took the town of
Southeast approximately five years to develop plans, receive
regulatory approval, obtain low cost financing and construct a new
permanent water supply system. During this lengthy period, the Town
incurred approximately $380,000 of extraordinary expenses for
operating and capital costs relating to water acquisition,
purification and disposal of water purification waste water, as well
as other related costs incurred to acquire and construct a new water
supply system. This bill would authorize the town to issue bonds to
repay its general fund for the extraordinary expenses incurred on
behalf of the water district for a term of up to thirty years in order
to minimize the fiscal impact on the water district's residents.

LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

New bill

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

None to the state

EFFECTIVE DATE:

Immediately.
